candidates.text:
Step by Step Working:
1. Create the kit. Click "Configure Kit/Pack", fill in the basic details (name, SKU, buyer, season and so on) and click "Create Kit".
2. Add the items. On the Pack Items tab, add each garment and choose its colours or sizes. Enter quantity and price.
3. Add packaging. On the Packing Materials tab, add bags, tickets, labels and so on.
4. Add labour. On the Routing/Processes tab, pick the packing process and its rate.
5. Add extra charges. On the Additional Cost tab, add things like freight.
6. Check the totals. On the Summary tab, see the total cost, type in the selling price, and check the profit.
7. Make size versions (optional). From the list, duplicate the kit into other sizes.
8. Approve. Click "Approve". The kit is now locked.
9. Auto Save. is also working.

3.2 Duplicate pop-up:
1. If the Ratio type is Size Ratio then while duplicating it will show colors to select, if Color Ratio then while duplicating it will show sizes to select & if Mixed ratio then while duplicating it will show colors & sizes to be selected. Multi- selection of colors & sizes is allowed.
2. The size list shows the sizes already used in the kit (or XS to XXL if there are none yet). Sizes that already have a child kit are hidden, so you can't create the same size twice.
3. Each new kit gets the next free Kit ID and is named "{master name} - {size}", for example "Boys Tee Kit - L".
4. Everything is copied from the master: items, packaging, labour and extra charges. Only the chosen size is kept on the items.
5. The new kit starts fresh: status is Open, actual quantity is 0, and you are recorded as its creator.
6. A child kit cannot be duplicated again. Only one level of copying is allowed.

chunks.title: Purpose
chunks.heading: Purpose
chunks.text:
A kit (or pack) is one product you sell that is made of several items — for example, a 5-pack of boys' t-shirts in one bag.
This feature lets the costing team work out how much one kit costs to make: the garments inside it, the packaging, the labour, and any extra charges like freight.
The user then types in a selling price, and the screen shows the profit.
When everyone agrees on the numbers, the kit is approved and locked so nobody can change it.
To price the same kit in other sizes, the user can duplicate it — one copy per size — instead of building each one from scratch.
chunks.locator: § Purpose

Wastage % | Extra material allowed for loss or damage. 2% wastage on 100 bags means you pay for 102.
Total Cost | Everything added up: items + packaging + labour + extra charges.
Profit % (Margin) | How much of the selling price is profit.
Markup % | How much the selling price is above the cost.
Open / Approved | The two statuses a kit can have. Open = still being worked on. Approved = final and locked.

chunks.title: 3.2 Duplicate pop-up
chunks.heading: Solution › Kit/Pack Screens › 3.2 Duplicate pop-up
chunks.text:
Use Case: making size versions of a kit quickly. Pick one or more sizes, and the system creates one new child kit for each size.
Duplicate pop-up: pick one or more sizes
Working:
• If the Ratio type is Size Ratio then while duplicating it will show colors to select, if Color Ratio then while duplicating it will show sizes to select & if Mixed ratio then while duplicating it will show colors & sizes to be selected. Multi- selection of colors & sizes is allowed.
• The size list shows the sizes already used in the kit (or XS to XXL if there are none yet). Sizes that already have a child kit are hidden, so you can't create the same size twice.
• Each new kit gets the next free Kit ID and is named "{master name} - {size}", for example "Boys Tee Kit - L".
• Everything is copied from the master: items, packaging, labour and extra charges. Only the chosen size is kept on the items.
• The new kit starts fresh: status is Open, actual quantity is 0, and you are recorded as its creator.
• A child kit cannot be duplicated again. Only one level of copying is allowed.

chunks.heading: Solution › Kit/Pack Screens › 3.3 Kit detail page › Tab 3 — Packing Materials (the packaging)
chunks.text:

Colour & Size should not be mandatory for packing material (If blank should be considered as None type dependency).

chunks.title: Tab 5 — Additional Cost (extra charges)
chunks.heading: Solution › Kit/Pack Screens › 3.3 Kit detail page › Tab 5 — Additional Cost (extra charges)
chunks.text:

Additional Cost: a freight charge of 25,000

chunks.title: Tab 6 — Summary (totals and profit)
chunks.heading: Solution › Kit/Pack Screens › 3.3 Kit detail page › Tab 6 — Summary (totals and profit)
chunks.text:
A view-only overview of the whole kit, plus the place to enter the selling price.
Summary: kit info, every cost line, and the totals
• Kit Information — kit ID, name, component type and ratio type.
• BOM Line Items — one line per item, packaging material, labour and extra charge.
• Totals — Total Cost, Selling Price (you type this), Discount % (you type this, but it doesn't affect anything yet), Profit %, Markup %, and BMV and EPM (always 0.00 for now).
• Approval Summary — on master kits only. Shows the master and all its child kits in one table.
Approval Summary on a master kit: KIT-381 and its child KIT-382
Approval summary Column- Kit, Kit- SKU, Kit-SKU Description, BOM Status, Total Cost, Selling Price/FOB, Profit %, Markup%, EMP.
chunks.locator: § Solution › Kit/Pack Screens › 3.3 Kit detail page › Tab 6 — Summary (totals and profit)

chunks.title: Messages the user will see – Table 7
chunks.heading: Solution › Messages the user will see
chunks.text:
Columns: When (text); Title (text); Message (text)
When | Title | Message
Deleting a kit (no children) | Confirm Deletion | {PackingKitID} will be deleted. This cannot be undone.
Deleting a master with children | Confirm Deletion | {PackingKitID} and its {N} duplicated child kit(s) will be deleted. This cannot be undone.
Delete worked | Deleted | {PackingKitID} was deleted.
Delete failed | Delete Failed | Could not delete the Kit/Pack.
List didn't load | Load Failed | Could not load Kit/Packs from the mock store.
One size duplicated | Kit Duplicated | {newID} was created from {masterID}.
Several sizes duplicated | Kits Duplicated | {N} kits created from {masterID}: {id, id, …}.
Duplicate failed | Duplicate Failed | Could not create the duplicate Kit/Pack(s).
Required fields missing | Cannot Create Kit | Fill in every required field first (Name, Kit SKU, Component Type, Ratio Type, Product Group, Sub-Category, UOM, Buyer, Buyer Dept, Season).
Kit created | Kit Created | {PackingKitID} was created.
Create failed | Create Failed | Could not create the Kit/Pack.
Auto-save failed | Save Failed | Could not save the Kit/Pack.
Kit doesn't exist | Not Found | That Kit/Pack does not exist. (then returns to the list)
"Copy From" clicked | Not Available Yet | Copying an existing Kit/Pack is not built in this proto yet.
